newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel sells Yozma venture capital fund.
newsitem.headline: Israel sells Yozma venture capital fund.

text.p: Israel said on Sunday it would sell the state-owned Yozma venture capital fund to Ofer Brothers Investments Ltd for 50 million shekels.
A statement released by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said eight groups had originally expressed interest in the offering but fewer had actually bid.
"Ofer Brothers bid was the highest," it said, noting it was in line with an outside expert's valuation of Yozma.
The sale included Star venture capital fund in which Yozma has holdings and Yozma's direct holdings in high-tech companies.
Yozma was formed in 1992 to encourage venture capital investment in Israel and help create employment for immigrants from the former Soviet Union then streaming into the country.
All told, it helped leverage $200 million in investments. But in recent years, the venture capital industry has thrived on its own, with more than $1 billion in capital raised.
As a result, the Treasury concluded direct government intervention was no longer needed and won approval from the parliamentary Finance Committee in October to sell Yozma.
